label: sound
instruction_covers: chunks(task, it, n, **options) and Task.chunks(it, n) build a signature whose group() is two starmap-style signatures split at the chunk size
calling the signature applies the generated group immediately and returns its result; apply_async publishes that group with the supplied options and routes it by the underlying task name
chunks.from_dict round-trips the stored task, iterable, chunk size and options
a built-in celery.chunks task accepts (task, it, n), builds the same signature in the current app, executes it and returns the result
from celery import chunks and the celery shell locals expose chunks alongside group, chain, xmap and xstarmap
notes: The base image's celery has no chunks class and does not export it (celery/__init__.py and celery/bin/shell.py list only chain, chord, group, xmap, xstarmap), so the engineer must add it. The structure the tests probe is the existing sibling convention: xstarmap is a celery.starmap signature whose kwargs are task and it, and _basemap.apply_async forwards route_name=task_name_from(self.kwargs.get('task')). The instruction explicitly says 'starmap-style' and 'route it using the underlying task name' and names xmap and xstarmap as the siblings to mirror, so the route_name kwarg and the celery.starmap kwargs are read off the repo, not invented. The idempotency, independence and repeated-construct tests assert ordinary per-instance behaviour that any correct implementation passes.
